## Purpose and Entry Points
R2R is a self-hostable, REST-oriented AI retrieval platform: multimodal document ingestion, hybrid/vector retrieval, RAG and research agents, knowledge graphs, and multi-user document/collection management. The Python server starts through `py/r2r/serve.py` and assembles the application in `py/core/main/app_entry.py` / `py/core/main/app.py`. Consumers use Python and TypeScript SDKs via `py/sdk/sync_client.py`, `py/sdk/async_client.py`, and `js/sdk/src/r2rClient.ts`.

## API and Application Assembly
Versioned HTTP endpoints are separated by resource domain—documents, chunks, collections, retrieval, graphs, conversations, users, prompts, indices, and system. Routers should remain thin API boundaries over services:
- `py/core/main/api/v3/documents_router.py`
- `py/core/main/api/v3/retrieval_router.py`
- `py/core/main/api/v3/graph_router.py`

`py/core/main/assembly/builder.py` and `py/core/main/assembly/factory.py` select and wire provider implementations from runtime configuration, allowing light/local versus full/deployed installations without changing service callers.

## Service Layer and Core Flows
Services contain use-case orchestration between routers, providers, and background workflows:
- `py/core/main/services/ingestion_service.py`
- `py/core/main/services/retrieval_service.py`
- `py/core/main/services/graph_service.py`

Primary ingestion flow is API/SDK request → ingestion service → file/ingestion provider and format parser → chunking/embedding → PostgreSQL-backed document/chunk/vector persistence; graph extraction can be scheduled from ingested content. Retrieval flows are API → retrieval service → database hybrid search and LLM/agent generation, returning search results or cited RAG output. Authorization, ownership, collections, limits, and prompts constrain these operations.

## Ingestion and Knowledge Construction
The parser layer supports media, structured, and text inputs, while provider interfaces isolate parser/ingestion implementations:
- `py/core/parsers/media/pdf_parser.py`
- `py/core/providers/ingestion/r2r/base.py`
- `py/core/providers/ingestion/unstructured/base.py`

Document text is split through shared abstractions, embedded through configured models, and stored as searchable chunks. Graph workflows perform entity/relationship extraction and community-oriented graph processing:
- `py/core/main/orchestration/hatchet/ingestion_workflow.py`
- `py/core/main/orchestration/hatchet/graph_workflow.py`
- `py/shared/abstractions/graph.py`

## Retrieval, RAG, and Agents
Retrieval combines semantic/vector and keyword-oriented database capabilities, with prompt-driven RAG and tool-using agents:
- `py/core/agent/rag.py`
- `py/core/agent/research.py`
- `py/core/providers/database/postgres.py`

Agent tools include knowledge/file search and web acquisition, creating an explicit boundary between tenant knowledge-base retrieval and internet-backed research:
- `py/core/base/agent/tools/built_in/search_file_knowledge.py`
- `py/core/base/agent/tools/built_in/web_search.py`
- `py/core/base/agent/tools/built_in/tavily_search.py`

## Provider and Persistence Boundaries
Abstract provider contracts in `py/core/base/providers/` decouple application logic from concrete integrations. Implementations cover PostgreSQL/pgvector data, S3 or PostgreSQL file storage, OpenAI/LiteLLM/Ollama/Anthropic/Azure model access, OCR, auth, email, and scheduling. Key implementations:
- `py/core/providers/database/postgres.py`
- `py/core/providers/embeddings/openai.py`
- `py/core/providers/llm/litellm.py`

PostgreSQL schema evolution is managed under `py/migrations/`. Authentication supports internal JWT/R2R auth and external Clerk/Supabase alternatives.

## Deployment and Runtime Topology
Light mode runs the Python service with local/simple providers. Full Docker and Kubernetes deployments provision R2R alongside PostgreSQL/pgvector, Hatchet orchestration with RabbitMQ, MinIO-compatible object storage, optional Unstructured parsing, and a separate graph-clustering service:
- `docker/compose.full.yaml`
- `deployment/k8s/kustomizations/kustomization.yaml`
- `services/clustering/main.py`

Hatchet is the durable asynchronous-workflow boundary for long-running ingestion and graph jobs; `simple` orchestration offers an in-process alternative. Production observability includes Fluent Bit configuration and optional Sentry integration.
